title: Are Two Stations Connected
real_world_story: A passenger wants to know whether they can travel from one station to another through any sequence of connections. The transit network is modeled as a directed graph. Use a depth-first traversal to determine whether the destination station is reachable from the origin station.

real_world_connection.algorithm_represents: Following connections as far as possible to discover whether travel is possible

problem_statement: Given a directed graph with N stations and M connections, and two nodes S and T, determine whether there is a path from S to T. Print YES if T is reachable from S, otherwise print NO.
task: Use DFS to check whether the destination station is reachable from the origin station.
input_format: The first line contains four integers N, M, S and T, where N is the number of stations, M is the number of directed connections, S is the origin station, and T is the destination station. The next M lines each contain two integers U and V indicating a directed connection from station U to station V.
output_format: Print YES if node T is reachable from node S, otherwise print NO.

examples.explanation: The passenger can travel 1 -> 2 -> 3 -> 4, and also 1 -> 2 -> 4.
There is no connection leading from station 1 toward station 4, so the destination is unreachable.

expected_algorithm.name: Graph DFS
expected_algorithm.reason: DFS explores one connected route as far as possible and can determine whether the target is reachable using recursion or an explicit stack.

hint: Begin the traversal at the origin station S.
Visit a neighbor and follow it as far as possible before backtracking.
If the destination station T is visited, it is reachable.
real_world_takeaway: DFS helps a transit system quickly confirm whether two stations are connected, identifying viable trips between parts of the network.
